the welded joint is characterized by a very good mechanical behaviour, both in terms of static and dynamic properties.
the welded joints show good mechanical properties, comparable to the parent materials, and a good fatigue behaviour.

the welded joints are characterized by an acceptable strength, ductility and fatigue behaviour, even if they are not comparable to the parent materials; in particular, the fatigue behaviour of the welded joint is comparable to the 7075 parent material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FSW technique is a suitable and effective joining method for dissimilar aluminium alloys, which allows to obtain welded joints with mechanical properties close to those of the parent materials, and with good fatigue resistance.

the FSW process is a very efficient technique to join dissimilar plates of aluminium alloys, even though the welded plates have shown a lower mechanical strength than the parent materials, but the fatigue endurance of the welded joints is very high.

the FSW technique is an efficient and effective way of joining the 2024– 7075 aluminium alloys, since a good joint efficiency has been obtained, even if the welded plates are dissimilar and have different mechanical properties.
